answer: Use a bonded attestation graph: every agent is a vertex linked only after peers verify its past work, and each link carries a small stake slashed on misbehaviour. A newcomer must earn endorsements over weeks, so an attacker cannot spin up thousands of identities at once; each fake vertex needs real work, time, and locked stake lost on fraud. The public signal is the graph itself: dense, long-lived connections are hard to fake cheaply, while a zephyr of fresh, unlinked identities with no history stands out and is throttled before it can vote or claim rewards.
